fixes.row: With Noah and every living creature
fixes.why: Rule 6: the first two examples say only 'you' (God speaking to Noah); the label's name is not in the verse, and this row, unlike the Abraham row, has no note saying who 'you' is.
fixes.fix: Add note: Gen 6:18 and 9:9 say 'you', God's speech to Noah, named in Gen 6:8 and 9:8.

fixes.row: Covenants made in Moab, at Shechem and in the days of Jehoiada, Asa, Hezekiah, Josiah and Ezra
fixes.why: Rule 6: the label names kings, but 2 Kgs 23:3 ('the king') and 2 Chr 15:12 ('they') do not name Josiah or Asa, so a reader of the example cannot see the label.
fixes.fix: Add note: 2 Kgs 23:3 is Josiah's (named in 23:1); 2 Chr 15:12 is Asa's (named in 15:8); 2 Chr 29:10 is Hezekiah's (named in 29:1).

fixes.why: The first example reads 'my house' and 'me' with no name in the verse; it is David's last words, named only at 2 Sam 23:1.
fixes.fix: Add note: 2 Sam 23:5 is David's own speech (named in 23:1).

fixes.row: With the day and the night, the beasts, the stones, one's eyes, death
fixes.why: The label is accurate, but Isa 28:15 is a scoffers' boast ('We have made a covenant with death') and Isa 28:18 says it will be annulled. With no note, a reader can take a covenant with death as a positive covenant.
fixes.fix: Add note: Isa 28:15 and 28:18 are the boast of scoffing leaders, 'a covenant with death', which the next verse says will be annulled; the page does not say more.

fixes.row: The covenant and loving devotion, mercy
fixes.why: Rule 6: the label's 'loving devotion' is not seen in Neh 9:32, which prints 'gracious covenant'. Unless the Hebrew there is the same word (ḥesed) and a note says so, the example does not show its label.
fixes.fix: Check Neh 9:32 in the word-by-word text. If the same Hebrew word stands there, add a note saying the Berean prints 'gracious' for it. If not, move the verse out of this row.

fixes.row: The blood of the covenant, the cup, the sacrifice
fixes.why: Rule 6: the label names the sacrifice, but none of the four shown examples says sacrifice; the sacrifice reading (Ps 50:5, 'a covenant with Me by sacrifice') is in the row but not shown first.
fixes.fix: Show Ps.50.5 among the four examples, in place of one of the blood verses, so the label's word is seen.

fixes.row: Between people and nations: made, sworn and forbidden
fixes.why: Deut 7:2 and Exod 23:32 forbid covenants with the peoples of the land, and Josh 9 is the Gibeonites' covenant. The row puts these beside David and Jonathan with no note saying who the peoples are. The label is accurate, but the missing context is what a reader of this row needs, and the rabbi and justice-attentive reader would be misled by an uncontextualised 'forbidden'.
fixes.fix: Add note: Deut 7:2 and Exod 23:32 name the peoples of the land (Canaan) as those with whom no covenant is to be made; Josh 9 is the Gibeonites' treaty, made by deceit (9:22); the prohibitions are as the text states them.

fixes.row: Broken, transgressed, forsaken, despised, profaned, corrupted; did not continue in
fixes.why: Hos 6:7 'like Adam' reads as a covenant-of-works allusion to Reformed and Lutheran readers, and the row sets it silently in the list of breaches. The page should say it takes no view.
fixes.fix: Add one line to the note: Hos 6:7 says 'like Adam' (or 'as men'); the page does not decide who or what Adam is there.

worker_points.point: 1. How the covenants relate: the block of rows 8-14 read as no ranking; is 'A new covenant; the first covenant, the old covenant' a ranking of new over old?
worker_points.why: The labels are in alphabetical order, each row carries the same no-side sentence, and the note quotes the text's own words. The rabbi's objection is to framing, which the note answers; the label is the text's.

worker_points.point: 2. Heb 8:7, 8:13, 9:1, 9:18 are not in the hub; does a reader miss them?
worker_points.why: The note of the new-covenant row says the Greek has no noun there and Heb 8:13 is a key verse. That is enough for a reader; the Berean's supplied 'covenant' should not be in a row without a noun.

worker_points.point: 3. Rom 11:27 sits in the catch-all, not the Israel row.
worker_points.why: The verse does not name Israel; the note says whom 'them' might be and that the page takes no side.

worker_points.point: 4. The row 'The covenants ... Jesus its guarantor and mediator' is by hand; does the label read as the text's?
worker_points.why: Each shown example carries the label's words (plural covenants, a better covenant, Jesus or Christ as guarantor or mediator). It is a by-hand divine-person row as the rules require, and the note names no doctrine.

worker_points.point: 5. Dan 9:27 kept in the blood-and-sacrifice row.
worker_points.why: The verse has covenant and sacrifice together, and the note says readers part on who 'he' is. It is a fit for the sacrifice label. The Catholic and Orthodox seats are served by the note, not by moving it.

worker_points.point: 6. Heb 9:16-17 as a two-verse 'will' row kept on purpose.
worker_points.why: One Greek word, two English senses, inside one passage; the row keeps the rule that one sense is never the whole word.

worker_points.point: 7. Abram row includes Gen 17 verses that say 'you'; the rabbi may want the covenant of circumcision noticed.
worker_points.why: The note says who 'you' is. The circumcision verses also sit in the sign row, which is the place for them.

worker_points.point: 8. Hos 6:7 'like Adam' in the Broken row.
worker_points.why: The worker asked for a note if wanted. Reformed and Lutheran readers will hear the covenant-of-works allusion, and one line stating the page takes no view is enough.

worker_points.point: 9. Between people and nations: label 'made, sworn and forbidden'; is Ps 83:5 misleading there?
worker_points.why: The label is accurate, but the forbidden verses need a note saying who the peoples are (fix above). Ps 83:5 is an alliance against God, a human covenant of the same kind; it is fine in the row.

worker_points.point: 10. Divine persons by hand; the 'Keep' row's note on eternal security.
worker_points.why: No row names God or the Spirit as a label, and the Keep note says nothing of what keeping earns or whether it can be lost, which the Wesleyan, Baptist and Pentecostal seats can accept.

worker_points.point: 11. Israel row 52 and ark row 49 verses dominate.
worker_points.why: The counts are the Hebrew's plain numbers; the rows do not favour a reading by size.

missing.what: Isa 42:6 'a covenant for the people and a light to the nations' (לִ + בְרִית), not seen by the builder; it belongs in the foreigners and nations row, and the rabbi and the justice-attentive reader would expect it there.

examples_checked: 20 of 25 labelled rows show their label in all four examples; the catch-all has no label. The five that do not: With Noah (Gen 6:18, 9:9 say 'you'); Moab and the kings (2 Kgs 23:3, 2 Chr 15:12 name no king); David (2 Sam 23:5 says 'my house'); loving devotion, mercy (Neh 9:32 prints 'gracious'); blood, cup, sacrifice (no example shows sacrifice).
summary: The hub is accurate to its verses and keeps the no-side rule on each contested point, and the no-side blocks read as no ranking. Five rows need a note or a changed example so that a shown verse carries its label, and the Between-nations row needs context for the forbidden peoples, so it ships after these fixes.
